operators.description: Scan all 100K supplier rows via dense_pk array, check s_comment for pattern, collect matching s_suppkey values into bitset(100001)

operators.predicate: p_brand <> 'Brand#45' AND p_type NOT LIKE 'MEDIUM POLISHED%' AND p_size IN (49, 14, 23, 45, 19, 3, 36, 9)
operators.description: Scan all 2M part rows via dense_pk array. p_brand and p_type are dictionary-encoded (uint8): resolve dict codes for 'Brand#45' and 'MEDIUM POLISHED*' prefix at init time, then compare codes. p_size checked against 8-element lookup array or bitset(50). Collect passing p_partkey into bitset(2000001). Also store (p_partkey -> group_key) mapping for aggregation.

Morsel-driven parallel scan of 8M partsupp rows. For each row: (1) check ps_suppkey NOT in complaint_suppkey_bitset (anti-join), (2) check ps_partkey in valid_partkey_bitset (semi-join with filtered part). Surviving rows (~1.2M): look up group_id from partkey_to_group_map[ps_partkey], then insert ps_suppkey into thread-local per-group bitset for COUNT(DISTINCT).
Merge thread-local hash_map<group_id, bitset<suppkey>> structures by OR-ing bitsets for same group_id across all threads. Then popcount each merged bitset to get supplier_cnt.
Sort ~18K result rows. Decode p_brand and p_type dictionary codes back to strings for output and for correct lexicographic sort order. Use std::sort on materialized result vector.
Final projection. p_brand and p_type output as decoded strings.

data_structures.partkey_to_group_map: direct_array(2000001, uint32_t) mapping p_partkey -> composite group_id (0 = not valid)
data_structures.group_id_encoding: composite of (p_brand_code, p_type_code, p_size) packed into uint32_t: brand_code * 256 * 64 + type_code * 64 + size_bucket

parallelism.notes: Only the partsupp scan+filter+aggregate (step 3) is parallelized — it processes 8M rows. Steps 1-2 are fast single-threaded setup (100K + 2M rows on in-memory arrays). Steps 4-6 operate on ~18K groups.

memory_estimate.thread_local_agg_per_thread: 18K groups * 12.5KB bitset = ~225 MB worst case per thread, but sparse allocation reduces this significantly
memory_estimate.optimization_note: Use compressed/sparse bitsets (roaring) for per-group suppkey tracking to reduce memory. Alternatively, since most groups have <100 distinct suppkeys, use small hash_sets that upgrade to bitsets only above threshold.

indexes_used.purpose: dense_pk array access for s_comment scan in step 1
dense_pk array access for part attribute filtering in step 2
